text: I will test whether the useful connection is not a generic relabeling into consistency/robustness, but an end-to-end separation of three errors: Bradley--Terry estimation noise around the LMM latent preference, semantic bias between that preference and true contribution/Shapley credit, and downstream policy distortion from reward shaping. I will check whether P proves only the first and whether Q supplies the interface/composition critique needed to expose the missing theorem.

Initial audit: the abstract-level mapping is too weak as stated. P, lines 363--376, bounds estimation of the LMM latent Bradley--Terry vector, not error to task-ground-truth credit or downstream return. Its Shapley bridge is conditional on the identity \(\mathbf c_t^*=\mathbf v_t^*\) (lines 383--389). Q explicitly says semantic outputs need a task-defined error and new proof (Q lines 260--265 and prediction-interface discussion), and cascaded component guarantees do not automatically transfer downstream (Q lines 1067--1109). The missing edge, rather than taxonomy relabeling, is the candidate contribution.

I will test a sharper line: decompose MARS-RA error into systematic comparator misspecification/bias plus finite-query estimation, propagate it through softmax and potential shaping, and determine whether any nontrivial policy/return guarantee is possible. I will also inspect whether PBRS telescoping makes the proposed downstream guarantee vacuous.

P proves only estimator concentration around the LMM latent vector, not robustness to semantically wrong comparisons: Proposition 1 assumes a connected graph and a Bradley--Terry comparator, then bounds \(\|\hat{\mathbf c}_t-\mathbf c_t^*\|_2/\sqrt n\le C_0\sqrt{n\log n/K}\) (P lines 361--376). Its Shapley link assumes away the missing bias via \(\mathbf c_t^*=\mathbf v_t^*\) and explicitly says it does not claim practical recovery (P lines 383--389). Thus increasing \(K\) removes sampling variance but cannot remove \(\|\mathbf c_t^*-\mathbf v_t^*\|\), despite the text describing hallucinations and inaccuracies as filtered. Q lines 345--350 and 1172--1179 require a task-defined prediction object/error and an end-to-end adapter analysis. This is a real gap, not a consistency--robustness relabeling.

Initial cross-reading: the abstract hypothesis overstates what P already proves. P, Sec. Theoretical Properties, Prop. 1 only bounds estimation of the LMM latent Bradley--Terry vector, \(\|\hat c_t-c_t^*\|\), under a connected graph and correctly specified stochastic comparator; P concludes convergence to the LMM latent preference, not to task credit. Prop. 2 reaches Shapley values only by assuming \(c_t^*=v_t^*\). Q, Sec. Semantic Predictions, says an LMM output needs a typed prediction object and error measure and that a compatible mechanism must account for adapter failures. Thus the missing quantity is semantic bias \(d(c_t^*,v_t^*)\), which repeated queries cannot remove.

Sharper joint question, changed from merely relabeling P: can one derive a cost-aware finite-training guarantee for MARS-RA that separates comparator variance, systematic semantic bias, and query cost? Candidate decomposition is task-credit error \(\|\hat c_t-v_t^*\|\leq \|\hat c_t-c_t^*\|+\|c_t^*-v_t^*\|\), with P supplying the first term \(O(\sqrt{n\log n/K})\) and Q insisting on prediction cost \(\kappa K\) and an explicit error interface. Critical caveat: because P uses potential-based shaping with terminal potential zero, shaping returns telescope; comparison quality affects finite-sample optimization, not the optimal-policy objective. A publishable theorem therefore needs sample complexity or regret, not the ordinary competitive ratio from Q.

Two sharper facts. First, for any trajectory ending with P’s zero terminal potential, \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\gamma^t F_t=-\psi(s_0,0)+\gamma^T\psi(s_T,T)=-\psi(s_0,0)\). Thus, conditional on the usual fixed initial-state convention, even arbitrarily wrong LMM credits do not alter optimal policies; they alter finite-training dynamics. A Q-style return-ratio consistency/robustness curve is therefore vacuous here. The meaningful target must be finite-training regret/sample efficiency versus semantic bias and query cost. Second, P’s Proposition 1 is not valid under its stated assumptions: with two agents and every observed comparison favoring agent 1, the undirected comparison graph is connected, yet the unregularized Bradley--Terry likelihood in P lines 325--328 has no finite MLE (the score gap diverges). P invokes regularized MLE in prose but specifies no regularizer; connectedness alone also does not provide uniform curvature without a bounded score range.

The initial scan’s proposed result, comparison error degrades reward-shaping guarantees, conflates two notions. Under exact episodic PBRS the optimal-policy guarantee does not degrade at all; only optimization/sample efficiency can. Conversely, P’s claimed rank-estimation robustness can fail before reaching that interface because its MLE may not exist and because repeated queries cannot remove semantic bias. Any publication should explicitly separate these claims.

Exact downstream check: P defines \(F_t=\gamma\psi_{t+1}-\psi_t\) and sets terminal \(\psi_T=0\) (Method, Potential Function). Hence \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\gamma^tF_t=-\psi_0+\gamma^T\psi_T=-\psi_0\). For a fixed initial state this cannot change the ordering of exactly optimized policies, irrespective of comparison accuracy. P experiments can still improve because shaping changes finite-time optimization. Therefore an end-to-end consistency claim about the optimal return would be vacuous; the meaningful joint target is performance after a fixed training budget, regret, or sample complexity.

P does not justify treating LMM errors as the sampling noise in Prop. 1. The proof needs a correctly specified Bradley--Terry comparator and concentration of its gradient; position-reversed calls to the same possibly deterministic LMM can have systematic, correlated, or cyclic errors. Connectivity alone cannot convert those into unbiased samples. Also the displayed proposition bounds \(\|\hat c-c^*\|_2/\sqrt n\) by \(C_0\sqrt{n\log n/K}\), while the appendix restatement bounds the unnormalized norm by \(O(\sqrt{n\log n/K})\); the normalization is inconsistent.

Concrete proposed frontier: if a new finite-training sensitivity lemma gives downstream penalty at most \(L\epsilon_K\), and \(\epsilon_K\leq b+A K^{-1/2}\) separates semantic bias \(b\) from sampling error, then adding Q-style query cost gives \(Lb+LAK^{-1/2}+\kappa K\), minimized continuously at \(K^*=(LA/(2\kappa))^{2/3}\). This predicts diminishing returns and a bias floor, directly matching P experiments across model accuracy and query count. The missing and genuinely hard step is proving \(L\) for MAPPO or a tractable MARL learner. Derivation: ada/derivation.tex.

Proposed concrete paper line, with the question changed: not ‘how does comparison error degrade MARS-RA’s asymptotic reward-shaping guarantee?’ but ‘under a fixed LMM-query budget, how do stochastic comparison variance and systematic semantic bias separately control finite-training performance?’ Theory should (i) replace P’s unregularized estimator by a well-posed regularized or constrained Bradley--Terry estimator, (ii) define the pseudo-true LMM score \(c_t^\dagger\) and task credit \(v_t^*\), yielding \(\|\hat c_t-v_t^*\|\leq O(\sqrt{n\log n/K})+b_t\) with \(b_t=\|c_t^\dagger-v_t^*\|\), and (iii) account for query cost \(\kappa K\). Experiments can hold marginal comparison accuracy fixed while contrasting independent flips with persistent pairwise reversals; the former averages away, the latter does not. P already exposes query-count/model-quality axes and dense task credit for evaluation (P lines 540--566, 665), making this test feasible. The downstream theorem must concern optimization regret or sample complexity, because episodic PBRS makes the optimal-policy comparison invariant.

Bottom line: there is a potentially publishable negative-to-constructive result, but Q alone does not supply the missing finite-training theorem. Its value is to force the correct typed error, cost accounting, and composition target. The smallest defensible contribution is a counterexample and corrected estimator/error decomposition plus controlled bias-versus-variance experiments; a stronger paper requires an algorithm-specific MAPPO convergence/regret analysis, which remains unresolved.

Cross-checking Grace entry 7 strengthens my objection: P calls the estimator ordinary MLE in Method and writes an unregularized negative log-likelihood. Connectedness does not ensure a finite Bradley--Terry MLE. For two agents with all \(K\) outcomes \(1\succ2\), the graph is connected but the likelihood is improved indefinitely as \(c_1-c_2\to\infty\). The prose appeal to regularized MLE does not repair the specified estimator because no penalty or bounded parameter set appears. Any use of P rate must first impose regularization or the standard no-separation condition, fix translation identifiability, bound dynamic range, and expose spectral-gap dependence.

My best account is now a qualified positive: reject generic LAA relabeling; develop a repaired, cost-aware finite-training theory separating semantic bias, comparator sampling or misspecification, graph design, and query cost. The most immediate publishable contribution may be a theory audit plus corrected estimator theorem and controlled experiments; the more ambitious contribution needs a finite-sample MARL sensitivity result. I will declare ready after one final ledger read.

Sharper result in emmy/end_to_end_audit.tex: after fixing Bradley--Terry translation invariance, task-credit error decomposes as semantic bias plus sampling error, \(\inf_a\|\hat{\mathbf c}_t-(\mathbf v_t^*+a\mathbf 1)\|/\sqrt n\le b_t+C_0\sqrt{n\log n/K}\). Softmax is \(1/2\)-Lipschitz in \(\ell_2\), so this propagates to potential error. Yet discounted PBRS telescopes, \(\sum_t\gamma^t(\gamma\psi_{t+1}-\psi_t)=-\psi_0+\gamma^T\psi_T\); with terminal potential zero this is policy-independent. Hence under exact optimization comparison quality cannot change the optimal policy. The observed dependence on model accuracy, \(K\), and \(\rho\) (P 550--552, 785--838) is necessarily a finite-training/optimizer effect, which P does not analyze. This changes the target question from an LAA competitive guarantee to finite-training stability/sample efficiency.

A second pair-specific gap: P defines \(\hat{\mathbf c}_t\in\mathbb R^{|I^t|}\) (316--329) and then uses it as a vector potential (337--349), while \(I^t\) changes. Per-agent PBRS telescoping requires persistent population-indexed coordinates and entry/exit boundary potentials; otherwise consecutive vectors may differ in dimension and \(\gamma\psi_{t+1}-\psi_t\) is not defined. P only later qualifies policy invariance under stationary transitions (642). A publishable extension can formalize open-team PBRS with entry/exit boundary terms, then study finite-training error rather than claim ordinary optimal-policy robustness.

Emmy’s entry 22 identifies the most pair-specific technical opening. My telescoping claim is valid only after defining a fixed-dimensional potential along the whole trajectory. P instead estimates \(\hat c_t\in\mathbb R^{|I^t|}\) while \(I^t\) changes, so \(\gamma\psi_{t+1}-\psi_t\) is dimensionally undefined across membership changes unless an embedding/boundary convention is supplied. For each agent whose active interval is \([\tau_i,\sigma_i)\), telescoping leaves entry/exit terms \(-\gamma^{\tau_i}\psi^i_{\tau_i}+\gamma^{\sigma_i}\psi^i_{\sigma_i}\); these need not be policy-independent. The strongest concrete paper is therefore an open-team PBRS theorem specifying population-indexed potentials and entry/exit conditions, followed by the bias/variance/query-cost finite-training analysis. This both tests and limits the earlier ‘PBRS is vacuously robust’ result.

Cross-check of Grace 7 and Ada 10/15: confirmed. P Method 325--328 specifies unregularized MLE; connectedness alone does not prevent complete separation, so a finite optimizer need not exist. Appendix 684 states \(\|\hat c-c^*\|=O(\sqrt{n\log n/K})\), line 744 derives \(O(\sqrt{\log n/K})\), while main line 367 states \(\|\hat c-c^*\|/\sqrt n\le C_0\sqrt{n\log n/K}\); these are mutually inconsistent in dimension. Appendix 699--704 also asserts local curvature with \(\mu\propto K\) while omitting a bounded dynamic range and explicit spectral factor. The repaired paper must use constrained or regularized BT, a gauge, and graph-dependent constants before any semantic/downstream analysis.

Emmy #22 qualifies my #9: P defines a fixed population \\(\\mathcal N\\) and an \\(n\\times n\\) comparison matrix (P 263, 285), but explicitly fits \\(\\hat{\\mathbf c}_t\\in\\mathbb R^{|I^t|}\\) only for active agents (316--329) and then subtracts consecutive softmax vectors in \\(F_t=\\gamma\\psi_{t+1}-\\psi_t\\) (337--347). If \\(I^{t+1}\\neq I^t\\), that displayed vector subtraction is ill-typed. My telescoping argument is valid only after specifying a common codomain and how shaped rewards are assigned through exit/re-entry. A natural repair embeds potentials in \\(\\mathbb R^n\\), e.g. \\(\\bar\\psi_i(s_t,t)=\\mathbf 1\\{i\\in I^t\\}\\,p_{t,i}\\), and applies every coordinate transition including entry/exit boundary terms. Omitting those terms breaks telescoping; including them restores objective invariance coordinatewise but creates possibly large boundary shaping signals whose finite-training effect must be analyzed. This is a particularly pair-specific interface failure because openness is P’s claimed advantage, while Q requires dynamic prediction timing/update semantics and proof across component edges (Q dynamic-prediction discussion and 1093--1109).

Revised best publication line: formalize open-team PBRS as the downstream interface, repair rank aggregation, then analyze finite-training sensitivity and query allocation. The core negative theorem/audit is two-layered: (i) P’s stated Bradley--Terry estimator is not well posed under connectivity alone and its error bound reaches only an LMM pseudo-truth; (ii) P’s active-set-valued potential is not defined across coalition changes. A corrected population-indexed construction restores exact optimal-policy invariance regardless of comparison error, so comparison quality can matter only through finite-training optimization and entry/exit transients. Then semantic bias \\(b\\), sampling term \\(AK^{-1/2}\\), and query cost \\(\\kappa K\\) yield the conditional frontier \\(Lb+LAK^{-1/2}+\\kappa K\\), with \\(K^*=(LA/(2\\kappa))^{2/3}\\), once a learner sensitivity bound \\(L\\) is proved. This is stronger and more pair-specific than generic consistency/robustness relabeling.

Best account: reject the scan hypothesis as too generic and partly ill-posed. The pair supports a sharper open-team PBRS paper: first prove when dynamic-membership, agent-indexed potentials preserve policy invariance and characterize entry/exit boundary terms; then repair BT estimation and separate finite-query variance from semantic bias and query cost. Fixed-dimensional episodic PBRS is invariant even under wrong comparisons, so ordinary return consistency/robustness is vacuous; membership changes can break that conclusion unless the interface is specified. A smaller publishable package is the counterexample to P Proposition 1, corrected estimator theorem, open-team PBRS theorem, and controlled independent-noise versus persistent-bias experiments. Unresolved: a genuine finite-training MAPPO sensitivity or regret bound \(G_N\); without it, the conditional frontier \(Lb+LAK^{-1/2}+\kappa K\) and \(K^*=(LA/(2\kappa))^{2/3}\) is a research target, not a proved result.

TeX-rendered restatement of #26--27: P fixes population \(\mathcal N\) and an \(n\times n\) matrix (263, 285), but fits \(\hat{\mathbf c}_t\in\mathbb R^{|I^t|}\) (316--329) and subtracts consecutive potentials (337--347), which is ill-typed when \(I^{t+1}\ne I^t\). Two repairs have different consequences. If shaping is paid only on active intervals, entry/exit boundary terms remain and can change policy ordering unless constrained. If every transition is instead defined in a common \(\mathbb R^n\) codomain, for example \(\bar\psi_{t,i}=\mathbf 1\{i\in I^t\}p_{t,i}\), and boundary transitions are paid, full-episode telescoping restores policy invariance but may inject large transient learning signals. Thus an open-team PBRS theorem must state the reward recipient and boundary convention before comparison-error robustness is meaningful. The subsequent conditional query frontier is \(Lb+LAK^{-1/2}+\kappa K\), minimized at \(K^*=(LA/(2\kappa))^{2/3}\); proving \(L\) remains unresolved.

After reading Ada #29, I agree that entry/exit boundary handling splits the result into two cases rather than simply invalidating telescoping. If rewards are paid only while an agent is active, the residual boundary terms can change policy ordering; if potentials and payments are defined in a common population-indexed codomain on every transition, full-episode telescoping restores policy invariance even for semantically wrong comparisons. This distinction should be the statement of the open-team PBRS theorem. It does not resolve the finite-training sensitivity constant \(L\), which remains the main obstacle to turning the conditional query frontier into a theorem.

Final type check sharpens entries 23 and 26. P defines the environmental reward as scalar at lines 337 and 347 but sets the potential to \(\operatorname{softmax}(\hat{\boldsymbol c}_t)\in\mathbb R^{|I^t|}\) at lines 316--345, so there are two undeclared interfaces: scalar-to-agent reward allocation and identification of vector coordinates when \(I^{t+1}\ne I^t\). A fixed-population potential \(\Phi_t\in\mathbb R^n\), with \(F_{t,i}=\gamma\Phi_{t+1,i}-\Phi_{t,i}\) applied on every transition, telescopes and restores invariance. Shaping only during each active interval \([\tau_i,\sigma_i)\) leaves \(-\gamma^{\tau_i}\Phi_{\tau_i,i}+\gamma^{\sigma_i}\Phi_{\sigma_i,i}\), potentially policy-dependent because P makes coalition transitions part of \(\phi\) (line 263). Q lines 1093--1109 explain exactly why a local guarantee cannot cross an unspecified edge. Full derivation: grace/open_team_pbrs.tex.
